candidate.title: CapSeq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina CapSeq schematic: enzymatic enrichment of formerly capped 5′ ends from total RNA, 5′ adaptor ligation, random priming, reverse transcription and purified cDNA. Gu et al. (2012) supports the long-capped-RNA CapSeq implementation. The target is CapSeq alone; CIP and TAP are depicted component operations, whereas the separate CIP-TAP small-RNA assay discussed in the same paper is not an alternative depicted target. The graph ends at the drawn cDNA product; primary-paper information explains how downstream DNA tags report RNA ends.

states.label: Total RNA with four depicted 5′ end classes
features: A mixed RNA input, represented by separate molecular-class icons: 5′ monophosphate (P), hydroxyl (OH), triphosphate (PPP), and guanosine-capped (GPPP) RNA.
These rows are end-chemistry classes in the total-RNA pool; no physical compartment separation or alternative assay branch is drawn.

The far-left overview repeats these end classes and highlights a short cap-proximal RNA segment in yellow. It is a descriptive icon alongside the CapSeq caption, not an additional material-processing step; the image supplies no color legend for the highlight.

evidence.locator: Total RNA column: four purple RNA classes labeled 5′ P, 5′ OH, 5′ PPP and 5′ GPPP
Far-left overview: repeated four end groups, with yellow highlight near the capped lower RNA 5′ end above the CapSeq explanatory caption

states.label: RNA pool after depletion of 5′-monophosphate RNA
features: The depicted 5′ P class is removed from the retained pool; 5′ OH, 5′ PPP and 5′ GPPP classes remain.
This is selective depletion, not proof that every structural RNA is absent.

evidence.locator: Terminator arrow and succeeding column: 5′ P class disappears; 5′ OH, 5′ PPP and 5′ GPPP remain
Experimental Procedures, RNA samples and library preparation, [b00064]
evidence.quote: RNA was extracted using TRI Reagent (MRC, Inc.) or phenol. For CapSeq, 0.5 – 2 μg of total RNA was treated with Terminator exonuclease (Epicentre) to degrade rRNAs, calf intestine phosphatase (CIP, NEB) to remove 5′ phosphates, and tobacco acid pyrophosphatase (TAP, Epicentre) to remove 5′ caps. The resulting long-capped RNAs were ligated to a 5′ adapter. First strand cDNA was primed using a pool of random octamers containing a common 5′ sequence corresponding to a 3′ adapter oligo. The first strand cDNA was size selected and then amplified using Illumina adapter oligos.

states.label: Dephosphorylated uncapped RNA plus still-capped RNA
features: The retained uncapped population is represented as 5′ OH; the preceding 5′ PPP class is no longer drawn separately.
The lower RNA retains its 5′ GPPP cap through CIP; its preparation history includes Terminator treatment.

states.label: Decapped 5′-monophosphate target RNA plus 5′-OH background
features: The formerly capped lower RNA now has a 5′ P end, creating the depicted substrate for adaptor ligation.
Uncapped RNA rendered or already bearing 5′ OH remains in the same treated pool; TAP does not turn this upper class into the lower target.

evidence.quote: The resulting long-capped RNAs were ligated to a 5′ adapter. First strand cDNA was primed using a pool of random octamers containing a common 5′ sequence corresponding to a 3′ adapter oligo.
evidence.rationale: Copying an adaptor-ligated RNA to its 5′ end links the cap-origin end to the primer-defined cDNA interface; this does not imply all random-primed products reach that end.

states.label: Purified cDNA endpoint representing CapSeq 5′-anchored tags
features: Single black line labeled cDNA; final strand number, end chemistry and internal purification steps are not drawn.
The primary implementation size-selects first-strand cDNA and subsequently amplifies it with Illumina adaptor oligos; PCR and sequencing are beyond the drawn endpoint.
The downstream sequenced carrier is DNA derived from enriched, formerly capped RNA 5′ ends; it is not the native capped RNA or an RNA-polymerase complex.

In the reported implementation, 70–90 nt tags identify candidate Pol II transcript starts and also capped trans-spliced ends. A capped end is not by itself proof of an original transcription-initiation site.
CapSeq targets longer capped RNAs, including primary miRNA transcripts; the schematic does not establish efficient capture of mature miRNAs or short capped piRNA precursors.
Enrichment does not establish absolute cap or biological specificity, full-transcript coverage, or complete structural-RNA removal.

operations.label: Terminator
operations.description: Treat total RNA with the named 5′-phosphate-dependent exonuclease; the depicted 5′ P RNA class is degraded and disappears from the retained pool. The other three end classes continue.
operations.mechanism: Terminator 5′-phosphate-dependent exonuclease; the card and primary paper identify rRNA depletion as its purpose.
operations.information_effect: Reduces abundant structural-RNA background before cap-end enrichment; no RNA sequence tag is introduced.

operations.label: CIP
operations.description: Remove 5′ phosphates from the surviving uncapped phosphorylated RNA. Its depiction changes from separate 5′ PPP and 5′ OH rows to a single 5′ OH class; the capped lower RNA remains capped.
operations.information_effect: Prevents the uncapped class depicted as 5′ OH from acquiring the 5′ adaptor at the later ligation interface, while preserving the capped substrate for subsequent TAP treatment.

operations.mechanism: Tobacco acid pyrophosphatase (TAP) removes 5′ caps; the image specifies the resulting P end.
operations.information_effect: Converts the selected cap history into a ligatable end; the cap is no longer physically present in the resulting library substrate.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and far-left image caption explicitly name CapSeq, and Gu et al. [b00064] reports the same Terminator → CIP → TAP → 5′ adaptor → random-octamer cDNA route. All seven local operations apply to this schematic-level implementation. The parallel molecular icons describe the composition of one sequentially treated RNA pool, not separately processed assay branches. Candidate collection page 86 has the different heading “Cap-Seq: CXXC Affinity Purification Plus Deep Sequencing” and an Illingworth CpG-island reference; despite a similar RNA cartoon it is not used to rename or assign a DNA affinity method to this record. Candidate page 87 is headed CIP-TAP and reuses a similar cartoon, but its text and Gu et al. [b00065] describe 3′ linker ligation before decapping of small RNA, a distinct workflow. Neither candidate heading expands the assigned CapSeq target.
